title: Pre-game declaration artifact
description: Every `required` entry below is mandated by the BOOK, not inferred from a template. `U-019` records that the example artifacts prove only that keys occur in the inspected bytes -- they establish no requiredness -- and `X-04` is what happens when a schema asserts more than the sources support: it validated a template and refused every real artifact. additionalProperties is TRUE because the book was asked directly and is NOT-SPECIFIED on whether extra non-contradicting fields are forbidden in the reporting artifacts. Refusing an opponent's declaration over a key no source forbids would fail rule 36's mutual audit for no reason.

groups.description: Both groups. Rule 49 wants four repository links across the pair, and p.78/183 wants the MCP addresses.

group_name.description: The book requires the group NAME alongside the group_id (p.39/104, 78/183). It is validated when present but NOT required here, because `protocol/declaration._group` does not yet emit it — and a schema that rejects the only artifact this repository can produce is the X-04 failure again. Tracked as M7-28; promote to required once the builder supplies it.

mcp_servers.description: Public addresses only. A URL carrying a credential breaches rule 39, which forbids secrets in the repository even when it is private.

github_commit.description: Rule 53, p.40/106: the exact commit of the code that plays. Hex-only, seven to forty characters. minLength alone was not enough -- the reference hard-codes the string 'unknown', which is exactly seven characters and passed a length check while identifying nothing.

game_ended_at.description: Null at lock time and filled post-game. The declaration is written and cryptographically locked BEFORE the first move, so the end time is not knowable when the artifact is created — requiring a string here would have made the schema reject the only artifact the builder can honestly produce. The key stays required so its absence is still a defect; only its value may be null until the series ends.

games_played_declaration.description: Rule 37, p.131/275: an accurate count of games actually played, declared at the start of each game. Rule 38 makes a false declaration absolute disqualification of the project, which is why the count is derived from emitted result artifacts rather than entered by hand.

links.description: M7-02: **resolved** filenames, never the naming pattern. The book writes the convention as `config_<game_id>_g<NN>.json` (inst/:3600-3602); copying that literal into an artifact points at a file that does not exist, and :2243 is explicit that each name is derived from the game_id so files from different games do not get mixed up. X-04 fixed this pattern in the config schema and left the declaration builder still emitting the placeholder, so the contract became right while the artifact stayed wrong — the declaration's own links would have failed the pattern its own bundle publishes. `config` and `log` accept a string OR an array: a series has one per sub-game, and an opponent emitting a single name is tolerated because U-019 does not pin the type.

llm_model.description: Rule 24 (Mandatory), p.39/104. Declared once, for this peer.

hardware.description: Rule 24, p.39/104 and inst/:1278, which lists Operating System first, then CPU, RAM and GPU/VRAM. Sanction for an incomplete spec is denial of eligibility for computational bonuses. Declared once, for this peer.
